primary_purpose: Determine whether the 15 load-bearing-quadrant ASKs from CORRECTION01 were real production residuals or artifacts of the harness deliberately withholding pathAuthorityEvidence.

PRODUCTION_EQUIVALENT_WITNESS exercises the real production composition (buildPathAuthorityEvidence -> commandHostAuthorization with realpath evidence -> resolveSessionHostAuthorization override) for cat README.md and git diff under effective YOLO. Both return ALLOW with host_mode_safe_only_rule source (path evidence positive match).
Dogfood witnesses now run in BOTH PRE (synthetic, no evidence) and POST (production-equivalent) compositions side-by-side, so BYPASS01 has a complete pre/post diff to consume.

It now composes the host authorization directly via commandHostAuthorization, so the only difference between PRE and POST is whether pathAuthorityEvidence is supplied.

load_bearing_quadrant_observed_results.post_ASK_root_cause: All 3 surviving POST ASKs are ls .factory with reason 'realpath-unresolved, hostReason=realpath-failed-enoent'. The harness's sandboxed authoring shell cannot realpathSync('.factory') because the directory is gitignored. The standard expectation is that a realpath-resolution of .factory on a normal user host would succeed and the rule would ALLOW, but that exact execution was NOT performed in this investigation.

key_finding_cautious_framing: POST_COMMAND_POLICY_RESIDUAL = 3 environment-specific .factory realpath failures (realpath-failed-enoent under the IDE sandboxed authoring shell; not exercised on an unsandboxed normal host). NO_GENERAL_COMMAND_POLICY_RESIDUAL = PROVEN for the representative production-equivalent corpus (38 commands across 7 families under effective YOLO + Seatbelt + no requires_approval; representative path-bearing commands like cat README.md and git diff ALLOW with host_mode_safe_only_rule source after realpath evidence positive match). Therefore BYPASS01 is de-queued -- the residual is environment-specific, not a general command-policy defect -- and the right next ACT is ACT-CLINEMM-EDITOR-TOOL-APPROVAL-FRICTION-RECON01 (which will capture one live prompt rather than install a bypass on the command seam).

decision.rationale: Under the production-equivalent composition, the load-bearing quadrant collapses from 15 ASK to 3 ASK. The 3 survivors are an environment-specific realpath-failed-enoent on the gitignored .factory directory under the sandboxed authoring shell; not exercised on an unsandboxed normal host. Representative production-equivalent path-bearing commands (cat README.md, git diff) ALLOW with host_mode_safe_only_rule source. Sufficient to de-queue BYPASS01 per reviewer verdict PASS_WITH_NONBLOCKING_RESIDUE C1:GO. The user-observed YOLO friction is most plausibly at the editor/write_file/apply_patch tool approval surface per upstream issue #13114.
decision.next_act_scope: Phase 0 -- capture one live YOLO confirmation UI and freeze: TOOL_NAME, TOOL_INPUT_KIND, YOLO_EFFECTIVE, SEATBELT_EFFECTIVE, UI_PROMPT_TYPE, PROMPT_OCCURS_BEFORE_OR_AFTER_TOOL_EXECUTION. Phase 1 -- trace the SdkController non-command tool approval callback at SdkController.ts:799..818 (shouldAutoApproveTool reads autoApprovalSettings.actions.editFiles / .editFilesExternally / MCP per-tool flags, session override); freeze TOOL_POLICY_SOURCE, SESSION_OVERRIDE_SOURCE, AUTO_APPROVAL_SETTINGS_SOURCE, REQUEST_TOOL_APPROVAL_CALLBACK, FINAL_UI_PROMPT_SEAM. Inspect editor / apply_patch / write-or-create-file-equivalent / MCP tool paths. Phase 2 -- exact RED on the live-prompt tool: YOLO + Seatbelt + tool request -> approval callback says ? -> UI prompt occurs? Possible outcomes: callback=ASK -> policy defect; callback=ALLOW but UI still prompts -> completion/UI seam defect; callback never reached -> seam moved. Only after that choose the repair. Per upstream SDK docs and upstream issue #13114 (YOLO auto-approves commands and reads but pauses after file creation), tool auto-approval is a separate surface from command policy.

rationale: Per the upstream reviewer (HALT_RED_NOT_REPRODUCED): 'Do not start by allowing all commands. Start by proving exactly which approval path is still firing in YOLO, and why.' CORRECTION01 closed the four load-bearing errors (decorative override axis, missing real-prompt reproduction, kernel over-gating, corpus count) but the 15 ASKs it surfaced were SYNTHETIC -- produced by the harness deliberately withholding pathAuthorityEvidence. CORRECTION02 runs the same corpus through the PRODUCTION-EQUIVALENT composition (buildPathAuthorityEvidence + realpath) and shows that 149/152 corpus cells ALLOW; the 3 survivors are an environment-specific .factory realpath-failed-enoent under the IDE sandboxed authoring shell (not exercised on a normal unsandboxed host). Per the reviewer's P2 correction, the verdict framing is conservative: NO_GENERAL_COMMAND_POLICY_RESIDUAL = PROVEN for the representative production-equivalent corpus; POST_COMMAND_POLICY_RESIDUAL = 3 environment-specific .factory realpath failures. Sufficient to de-queue BYPASS01 (the residual is environment-specific, not a general command-policy defect). Next ACT is ACT-CLINEMM-EDITOR-TOOL-APPROVAL-FRICTION-RECON01, which captures one live YOLO prompt at the actual UI surface (per upstream issue #13114 the user-observed prompt occurs after file creation) and only after that scopes a bounded repair.
